_comment: Batch 12 (Sets 22-23). Distractor-only rewrites to remove the longest-answer cue. Correct options, stems, and rationales are unchanged; each distractor keeps its original meaning and stays wrong for the same reason. PN-S23-24 (handwashing times) is in skipped.json as numeric.

RN-S22-01.B: A client with a healing venous leg ulcer who is due for the weekly dressing change and reports no new pain
RN-S22-01.C: A client with type 2 diabetes who needs a monthly medication review and whose recent glucose readings have been stable
RN-S22-01.D: A client recovering from a total hip replacement who has a scheduled physical therapy visit at home later in the afternoon

RN-S22-02.A: "Take a nitroglycerin tablet under your tongue whenever you have any chest pain or chest pressure."
RN-S22-02.C: "Take a hot sauna every day to relax your heart and lower your blood pressure."
RN-S22-02.D: "Letting yourself become a little dehydrated will actually help improve your heart symptoms."

RN-S22-03.A: "No special precautions are needed for you, since a routine dental cleaning doesn't affect a prosthetic heart valve at all."
RN-S22-03.C: "You should avoid all dental care, including routine cleanings, for as long as you have the prosthetic valve."
RN-S22-03.D: "Stop taking your anticoagulant for a full week before the cleaning, without asking your provider about it."

RN-S22-04.A: "The Tdap vaccine protects you from tetanus only, in case you get a deep cut or a tear while you're delivering your baby at the hospital."
RN-S22-04.C: "You only need the Tdap vaccine if you've never had a dose of it before at any time in your life, so check your records."
RN-S22-04.D: "The Tdap vaccine should be given after you deliver instead, so that it doesn't affect your baby during the pregnancy."

RN-S22-05.A: "Stay seated for the entire flight with your seatbelt fastened, so that you don't fall in the aisle during any turbulence."
RN-S22-05.C: "Take a sleeping pill right after takeoff so that you can sleep comfortably through most of the long flight."
RN-S22-05.D: "Cross your legs at the knees or ankles to stay more comfortable in the small airplane seat for the long flight."

RN-S22-07.A: "No routine blood tests will be needed while you're taking carbamazepine, since it's a well-tested drug."
RN-S22-07.C: "Drink a large glass of grapefruit juice with each dose of carbamazepine to help your stomach tolerate it."
RN-S22-07.D: "Stop taking the carbamazepine right away on your own if it makes you feel drowsy or tired during the day."

RN-S22-08.A: A full replacement dose of levothyroxine starting on the very first day to correct the levels quickly
RN-S22-08.C: Stopping all of the client's cardiac medications while the levothyroxine is being started
RN-S22-08.D: Taking each dose of levothyroxine with a calcium supplement to improve its absorption

RN-S22-09.A: Try feeding the newborn again more slowly, using a different nipple and stopping to burp more often during the feeding
RN-S22-09.C: Offer sterile water instead of formula for the next feeding to see whether it is tolerated
RN-S22-09.D: Place the newborn in the prone position and continue the feeding slowly in small amounts

RN-S22-10.A: Fluid overload with peripheral edema and crackles in the lungs
RN-S22-10.C: Hyperkalemia only, with peaked T waves
RN-S22-10.D: Hypertension from excess fluid in the vascular space

RN-S22-11.A: Reassure the family that new confusion and constipation are a normal part of aging
RN-S22-11.C: Increase the oxybutynin dose to better control the bladder
RN-S22-11.D: Add a sedative at bedtime to help manage the confusion

RN-S22-12.A: "Stay in bed for the next 2 weeks so that your back has enough time to rest and heal completely."
RN-S22-12.C: "Avoid all movement and activity until the pain in your back is completely gone."
RN-S22-12.D: "Start lifting heavy objects every day so that the muscles in your back get stronger."

RN-S22-13.A: Give the full dose rapidly by IV push to shorten the amount of time that the client is exposed to the drug overall
RN-S22-13.C: Give the iron dextran by IM injection instead of IV, using the Z-track method
RN-S22-13.D: Mix it in the same IV bag with the client's other scheduled IV medications to save time

RN-S22-14.A: Have the client walk around immediately to prevent stiffness
RN-S22-14.C: Remove the dressing after 10 minutes to inspect the site
RN-S22-14.D: Place a heating pad on the site to relieve soreness

RN-S22-15.A: "You are not at any increased risk of infection now, since your liver and other organs will take over the spleen's job."
RN-S22-15.C: "Avoid all vaccines from now on, especially in the first year after surgery."
RN-S22-15.D: "A fever is expected for several months after this surgery, so don't worry about it."

RN-S22-16.A: Administer the bupropion as prescribed with the client's breakfast tray and then document that it was given
RN-S22-16.C: Give the bupropion with a small amount of alcohol to improve how well it is absorbed
RN-S22-16.D: Double the first dose so that the client's mood improves more quickly than usual

RN-S22-17.A: "Stop breastfeeding immediately and switch your baby to formula until the infection has cleared completely."
RN-S22-17.C: "Bind your breasts tightly with an elastic wrap to reduce the swelling and slow down milk production."
RN-S22-17.D: "Feed your baby only from the unaffected breast until the fever and redness are completely gone."

RN-S22-18.A: Insulin needs gradually decrease throughout the pregnancy and then rise again after delivery
RN-S22-18.C: Insulin needs usually stay the same throughout pregnancy and after delivery
RN-S22-18.D: Insulin is usually stopped in the third trimester and replaced with diet control to protect the fetus

RN-S22-19.A: "The levothyroxine is only needed for the first few months, until your baby's own thyroid gland starts working normally again on its own."
RN-S22-19.C: "Crush the tablet and mix it into a full bottle of soy-based formula, which helps the medicine absorb better."
RN-S22-19.D: "If your baby is sleeping at the usual dose time, skip that day's dose and just give it the next day instead."

RN-S23-01.B: A client who reports incisional pain of 6/10 and is asking when the next PRN analgesic dose is due
RN-S23-01.C: A client who is shivering after surgery and asking the nurse for a warm blanket and a sip of water
RN-S23-01.D: A client who is drowsy but arousable to voice, with SpO2 96% on room air and a steady respiratory rate

RN-S23-03.A: The client opens the eyes and responds appropriately to verbal commands
RN-S23-03.C: HR decreases from 84 to 76/min during the procedure
RN-S23-03.D: The client reports feeling relaxed and a little sleepy

RN-S23-05.A: "Take both medications together during the first week of the switch."
RN-S23-05.C: "Take the sacubitril-valsartan only on days when you feel short of breath."
RN-S23-05.D: "Increase your potassium intake with bananas and orange juice."

RN-S23-06.A: Infuse it slowly over 10 minutes through a peripheral IV line using an infusion pump, then flush the line with saline
RN-S23-06.C: Give it by intramuscular injection into the deltoid muscle and monitor the rhythm
RN-S23-06.D: Mix it in a 250-mL bag of D5W and infuse it slowly over about 1 hour by pump

RN-S23-07.A: Normal breathing pattern after blunt chest trauma
RN-S23-07.C: Pleural effusion from the rib fractures
RN-S23-07.D: An acute asthma attack triggered by the trauma

RN-S23-09.A: "Eat three large, high-fiber meals each day with water."
RN-S23-09.C: "Lie down right after eating to help with digestion."
RN-S23-09.D: "Drink carbonated beverages with meals to help settle your stomach."

RN-S23-10.A: Stop the tube feeding permanently and ask the dietitian to switch the client to a different plan of nutrition that does not use the feeding tube
RN-S23-10.C: Give a dose of an antidiarrheal medication such as loperamide immediately to control the loose stools
RN-S23-10.D: Double the volume of the free-water flushes every 4 hours to replace the fluid being lost in the loose stools

RN-S23-11.A: "Ibuprofen is the safest pain reliever for someone with kidney disease like yours, so you can take it whenever your knee is bothering you at all today."
RN-S23-11.C: "You can take double doses of ibuprofen on days when your knee pain is worse, since that will give you better relief."
RN-S23-11.D: "NSAIDs such as ibuprofen actually help protect your kidneys from further damage, so they're a good choice for you."

RN-S23-12.C: Improved mobility in the affected joint

RN-S23-14.A: "Palliative care and hospice are exactly the same type of care. The two names are used interchangeably, and both are offered to anyone with a serious illness at any stage, whether or not they want curative treatment."
RN-S23-14.C: "Choosing palliative care means that you are giving up on treatment. Once you start it, you will no longer receive any medications or care for your heart failure itself."
RN-S23-14.D: "Hospice is only available to people who have cancer. It would not be an option for someone with heart failure like you, even if your illness reaches its final stages."

RN-S23-15.A: "The fluid inside the blisters is what spreads the rash, so keep them covered and avoid touching other people until they dry up and heal."
RN-S23-15.C: "You'll need to be isolated at home and stay away from other people until the rash has cleared up completely."
RN-S23-15.D: "Scratching and opening the blisters will actually help the rash heal faster, because it lets them dry out sooner."

RN-S23-17.B: Tell the child that starting the IV won't hurt at all, so that the child stays calm and still
RN-S23-17.C: Have several staff members hold the child down firmly on the bed so that the IV can be started quickly
RN-S23-17.D: Give the child an IM opioid injection about 30 minutes before the IV is started to dull the pain

RN-S23-18.A: Continue the warfarin at the current dose to prevent a new clot or another stroke from forming in the brain
RN-S23-18.C: IV alteplase given as soon as possible to dissolve the clot and restore blood flow to the affected areas of the client's brain
RN-S23-18.D: Daily aspirin to prevent another stroke, started as soon as the client passes the swallow screening test

RN-S23-19.A: "Your child is in denial about Grandpa's death, which isn't normal at this age, so your child needs to start seeing a therapist right away for counseling."
RN-S23-19.C: "It's best to tell your child that Grandpa is sleeping peacefully now, since that is much easier for a young child to understand."
RN-S23-19.D: "It's best to avoid talking about Grandpa's death with your child until your child is old enough to understand what death means."

RN-S23-24.A: Stop the norepinephrine infusion and notify the provider of the low MAP
RN-S23-24.C: Give a 2-L bolus of normal saline as quickly as possible to raise the MAP
RN-S23-24.D: Wait 2 hours and then recheck the client's BP before making any changes to the infusion

PN-S22-01.A: "Lie flat in bed and breathe rapidly and shallowly through the mouthpiece until it's done."
PN-S22-01.C: "Take a deep breath and then hold it for the entire treatment, so the medicine stays in your lungs longer."
PN-S22-01.D: "Use the nebulizer only while you are up and walking around, so that your lungs stay open."

PN-S22-02.A: Within 12 hours after the injection, by measuring the size of the area of redness in millimeters
PN-S22-02.C: At 1 week after the injection, by asking the client whether the site has been itching
PN-S22-02.D: Only if the client later reports symptoms such as a persistent cough or night sweats

PN-S22-03.A: "Take your blood pressure right after you finish your morning coffee, so that you get a consistent reading each day."
PN-S22-03.C: "Cross your legs at the knees during the reading to keep yourself steady and comfortable in the chair."
PN-S22-03.D: "Take the reading with the cuff placed over a thick sweater or sleeve, so that it doesn't pinch your skin."

PN-S22-04.A: Behind the inner ankle bone, just below the medial malleolus
PN-S22-04.C: Behind the knee, deep in the popliteal space with the knee slightly flexed
PN-S22-04.D: In the groin, midway between the hip bone and the pubis

PN-S22-06.C: Glasgow Coma Scale for measuring level of consciousness
PN-S22-06.D: Braden Scale for pressure injury risk

PN-S22-07.A: The top of the handle reaches the level of the client's waist when the client stands upright with the arm bent at 90 degrees
PN-S22-07.C: The top of the handle reaches the height of the client's shoulder, so the client can lean the full body weight on it with a straight arm when walking
PN-S22-07.D: The cane is adjusted to be as tall as possible, so that the client is forced to stand up straight while walking with it

PN-S22-08.A: Pull the client up in bed by the weak left arm when repositioning them
PN-S22-08.C: Let the left arm hang freely at the side while the client is sitting up
PN-S22-08.D: Apply a tight sling to the left arm at all times, even while the client is in bed

PN-S22-09.A: Insist on a full shower immediately so that the resident's usual bathing schedule is kept and the daily routine is not disrupted at all
PN-S22-09.C: Bathe the resident as quickly as possible with cool water so that the bath is finished before the agitation gets worse
PN-S22-09.D: Have several staff members hold the resident still in the shower chair so that the full bath can be completed today

PN-S22-10.A: Wipe the fingertip with lotion to soften the skin first
PN-S22-10.C: Use the first drop of blood after squeezing the finger hard
PN-S22-10.D: Leave the alcohol wet on the skin when puncturing

PN-S22-11.A: "Aim to lose about 10 pounds every week so that you reach your goal weight quickly."
PN-S22-11.C: "Stop eating solid food completely until you reach your goal weight, and drink only water."
PN-S22-11.D: "Weight loss should never be a health goal, so try to focus on other things instead."

PN-S22-12.A: Fiber supplements alone, without any increase in the client's daily fluid intake
PN-S22-12.C: No bowel treatment at all until the client actually becomes constipated
PN-S22-12.D: Stopping the oxycodone so that the client's bowels return to normal

PN-S22-13.A: "The urine leakage is permanent after this type of surgery, so you will need to wear pads for the rest of your life."
PN-S22-13.C: "Limit your fluids to about 500 mL a day so that you leak less often while you're healing."
PN-S22-13.D: "You will need to use an indwelling catheter permanently to manage the leakage from now on."

PN-S22-14.A: "Apply deodorant and body powder beforehand so that you stay fresh and dry during the exam."
PN-S22-14.C: "Don't eat or drink anything for 12 hours before the mammogram, starting the night before."
PN-S22-14.D: "Drink the contrast solution about an hour before the test so that the images come out clearly."

PN-S22-15.A: "Douche on the morning of the test so that the vaginal area is as clean as possible for the provider's exam."
PN-S22-15.C: "Try to schedule the Pap test during the heaviest days of your menstrual bleeding."
PN-S22-15.D: "Apply a vaginal cream the night before the test to soothe the area and prevent discomfort."

PN-S22-16.A: Mild breast tenderness during the first month or two of taking the pills
PN-S22-16.C: Lighter menstrual periods with less cramping than before starting
PN-S22-16.D: Mild nausea during the first few weeks of taking the pills

PN-S22-17.A: "It's fine to have a drink or two of alcohol in the evening while you're taking this medicine for the infection."
PN-S22-17.C: "Your partner doesn't need to be treated, since only you are having symptoms of the infection."
PN-S22-17.D: "You can stop taking the medicine as soon as your symptoms start to improve, to avoid side effects."

PN-S22-18.B: "Any fever after the shots means that the vaccines didn't work, so your child will need to get all of the same shots again at the next visit."
PN-S22-18.C: "Side effects never occur with routine childhood vaccines, so you won't need to watch your child for anything at all afterward."
PN-S22-18.D: "Give your child children's aspirin every 4 to 6 hours for any fever, fussiness, or soreness at the injection sites."

PN-S22-19.A: "I can stop getting the shots whenever I start to feel better and the voices go away."
PN-S22-19.C: "Each shot only works for about a day, the same way that my pills did."
PN-S22-19.D: "I'll keep taking extra pills at home along with the shots, just to be safe."

PN-S22-20.A: Feeling tired from getting up every few hours at night to feed and change the baby
PN-S22-20.C: Occasional tearfulness and moodiness during the first week after the birth that went away on its own
PN-S22-20.D: Enjoying time with the baby and looking forward to visits from family and friends

PN-S22-21.A: "Add extra water to each bottle to make the can of formula last longer."
PN-S22-21.C: "Save any leftover formula from a feeding in the refrigerator and use it again the next day."
PN-S22-21.D: "Add a little rice cereal to the bottle at night to help the baby sleep longer."

PN-S22-22.A: "Start adding a small amount of rice cereal to your baby's bottle at about 2 months of age, and then slowly increase the amount every week as your baby grows bigger."
PN-S22-22.C: "Wait until your baby's first birthday before starting any solid foods at all, and keep giving only breast milk or formula until that time."
PN-S22-22.D: "Offer whole peanuts and tree nuts as some of the first foods, so that your baby gets used to them early and is less likely to develop an allergy."

PN-S22-23.A: "Apply a generous layer of regular adult sunscreen all over your baby's body every time you go outside, even if you plan to stay in the shade the entire time you're outdoors."
PN-S22-23.C: "Letting your baby get a few brief, mild sunburns early in the season will help build up the skin's tolerance to the sun for the rest of the summer."
PN-S22-23.D: "Rub a little tanning oil on your baby's arms and legs before going outside to keep the skin moisturized while you're out in the sun."

PN-S23-01.A: The client's dentures have been removed and stored safely
PN-S23-01.C: The client's ID band is in place on the left wrist
PN-S23-01.D: The client voided in the bathroom before transport

PN-S23-02.A: "Try to avoid coughing after surgery so that your incision doesn't open up."
PN-S23-02.C: "Cough only once a day, first thing in the morning, to clear out your lungs."
PN-S23-02.D: "Lie flat on your back while you cough so that the muscles around your incision stay relaxed."

PN-S23-03.A: Have the client stand up quickly in one smooth motion, before any lightheadedness or dizziness has a chance to set in
PN-S23-03.C: Walk the client all the way out to the hallway immediately to start building strength
PN-S23-03.D: Let the client walk to the bathroom alone this first time to promote the client's independence

PN-S23-04.A: "Peel the strips off after the first day so that the incision can air out and breathe."
PN-S23-04.C: "Soak the incision in a warm bath every day so that it stays clean and heals faster."
PN-S23-04.D: "Apply a moisturizing lotion over the strips every day to keep the skin around them soft."

PN-S23-05.A: A regular diet first, then switching to clear liquids only if the client becomes nauseated again
PN-S23-05.C: Full liquids only for the next 2 weeks after surgery, then a regular diet
PN-S23-05.D: Solid foods such as crackers first, to settle the stomach before giving any liquids

PN-S23-06.A: "You can safely return to your usual heavy lifting at work starting tomorrow morning if you feel up to it."
PN-S23-06.C: "Cough forcefully several times every day to keep your lungs clear after the surgery."
PN-S23-06.D: "Limit how much you drink for the first week after surgery to reduce the swelling."

PN-S23-07.A: "Blow your nose forcefully several times a day to clear out the drainage."
PN-S23-07.C: "Bend over to pick up heavy items as you normally would."
PN-S23-07.D: "Take aspirin as needed for pain after the surgery."

PN-S23-08.A: "Your child can share towels with brothers and sisters, as long as the towels are washed weekly."
PN-S23-08.C: "Have your child rub their eyes gently with their fingers to remove the crusty drainage."
PN-S23-08.D: "Use the same tissue to wipe both of your child's eyes so that you don't waste tissues."

PN-S23-09.A: "Clean your ear canals every day with cotton swabs after you swim or take a shower."
PN-S23-09.C: "It's fine to swim without drying your ears afterward, since the water will drain out on its own."
PN-S23-09.D: "Use a clean hairpin to gently scoop out any earwax that builds up in the ear canal."

PN-S23-10.A: "Applying an antifungal cream to the scalp twice a day will be enough to cure the ringworm."
PN-S23-10.C: "Shave your child's head completely so that the antifungal medicine can reach the skin of the scalp better."
PN-S23-10.D: "You can stop giving the medication as soon as your child's scalp starts to look better."

PN-S23-11.A: "Avoid all foods and supplements that contain calcium, since your body isn't able to handle dairy products anymore."
PN-S23-11.C: "Drink more regular milk each day, a little at a time, to slowly build up your tolerance to lactose."
PN-S23-11.D: "Calcium isn't really important for adults, since it's only needed by children whose bones are still growing."

PN-S23-12.A: "Vitamin C, since it supports immune function and helps absorb iron from plants"
PN-S23-12.C: "Sodium, since it is needed for fluid balance and nerve function"
PN-S23-12.D: "Fiber, since it supports regular bowel movements and heart health"

PN-S23-14.A: Lower both side rails while working so that you can reach the client easily from either side of the bed without stretching
PN-S23-14.C: Leave the bed in its highest position when finished, so that it is at a good height for the next linen change
PN-S23-14.D: Have the client get up and stand barefoot on the floor next to the bed while the linens are being changed

PN-S23-15.A: Collect the stool sample from the toilet water after the client has a bowel movement, using a clean plastic spoon from the kit
PN-S23-15.C: Refrigerate the specimen for 2 days before sending it to the lab so that more of the parasites can be seen
PN-S23-15.D: Mix the stool sample with some tap water in the container so that the lab can examine it more easily

PN-S23-16.A: Right after a large meal, when the client is feeling relaxed and comfortable
PN-S23-16.C: Only when the pouch starts to leak, so that supplies are not wasted
PN-S23-16.D: At bedtime, after the client has finished eating dinner for the day

PN-S23-17.A: "Put the used needles in your regular kitchen trash, inside a plastic grocery bag that is tied shut, and then take the trash out to the curb on the regular trash day."
PN-S23-17.C: "Recap each needle carefully after you use it, and then throw the capped needles away in the regular household trash can."
PN-S23-17.D: "Flush the used needles down the toilet one at a time, so that no one in your home or at the landfill can get stuck by them."

PN-S23-18.A: A 6-week course of oral vancomycin taken by mouth every day before the scheduled surgery
PN-S23-18.C: No treatment is needed, since colonization is not an infection
PN-S23-18.D: Alcohol-based hand rub applied inside both nostrils twice a day for a week

PN-S23-19.A: "Do you drink more alcohol than most of your friends do?"
PN-S23-19.C: "What is your favorite alcoholic drink to have with dinner?"
PN-S23-19.D: "Do you drink alcohol only on the weekends with friends?"

PN-S23-20.A: As a sign of a possible developmental delay, which should be reported to the provider so that further developmental testing can be arranged soon
PN-S23-20.C: As possible evidence of abuse at home, since an infant who is well cared for should be comfortable being held by anyone
PN-S23-20.D: As an allergic reaction to something in the exam room, such as the latex gloves or the cleaning products used on surfaces

PN-S23-21.A: Black, sticky stools that continue for the first 2 weeks after birth and then change to firm, brown, formed stools
PN-S23-21.C: Clay-colored or pale stools that are firm and formed by the end of the first week
PN-S23-21.D: Bright red or red-streaked stools that appear after the first few days of breastfeeding

PN-S23-23.A: Taking hot showers several times a day to help relieve the itching
PN-S23-23.C: Rubbing alcohol applied to the rash several times a day to help dry out the blisters
PN-S23-23.D: Breaking the blisters so that the fluid can drain and the rash can heal
